Commentary: Kuldeep Yadav to Romario Shepherd, FOUR, short and wide, hit me ball and Shepherd reaches out to slap it hard past cover-point and that's 24 runs plundered off this over
Arshdeep Singh [3.0-0-28-0] is back into the attack
Arshdeep Singh to Shai Hope, 1 run, good low full toss on the leg stump, clipped to long-on
Arshdeep Singh to Romario Shepherd, 1 run, yorker down the leg-side, clipped behind square for a run
Arshdeep Singh to Shai Hope, 1 run, low full toss, driven hard down the ground. Tilak cuts across from long-on and keeps it to one
Arshdeep Singh to Romario Shepherd, SIX, full tosses will be shown no mercy! Just waits for the ball to come and lofts it over mid-wicket so effortlessly. The belief is fading for the Indian fans

Arshdeep Singh to Romario Shepherd, FOUR, the bumper down the leg-side with no fine leg in place and Shepherd rocks back to help the pull fine to get it close to run-a-ball now. Looks like the fielder forgot to move himself to fine leg

Arshdeep Singh to Romario Shepherd, FOUR, it's short and wide of off now with no third man. The slower delivery from Arshdeep Singh, Shepherd swings, gets a thick edge that clears the infield and only 10 needed off 12 now
Axar Patel [3.0-0-51-0] is back into the attack
Axar Patel to Shai Hope, SIX, he moves to 96 and West Indies need 4 to win. Flighted delivery on the stumps, Hope gets down on one knee and muscles the slog sweep over long-on
Axar Patel to Shai Hope, no run, flatter delivery on the stumps, Hope punches it to cover

Axar Patel to Shai Hope, SIX, and he decides to end it with a six and finish by recording his 2nd T20I hundred. The West Indies have pulled off their highest successful run chase in T20Is. This is also the second quickest hundred for West Indies in this format. Shai Hope is absolutely pumped, does a double first pump and celebrates with his partner at the crease. Full and outside off stump, Hope reached out to loft this over long-off. From 5/2 to hunting down 250 with 9 balls to spare, this is sensational stuff from the West Indies

Rutherford 2/2: [What was the chat during your partnership with Shai Hope?] Honestly, it was just about enjoying it. When I went to him, I said, Listen, let's just try and bat as much balls as we could. I'm naturally a fast scorer. I naturally love to take the game on. So I didn't want to run away from that. So it was important for me to just play my game, and I know that once he is there also, it's even better because I can be as free as I could, and he gonna be there till the end. [On Shai Hope] I don't think there's much words to describe him. He is a phenomenal player. Even I look at him and I'm like, oh, how can you do it so steady so often? And I look at him and he inspires me a lot to work hard. Even when he's in the nets, I try to look at him. I try to take as much information. But I mean, the way he's doing, he needs credit. I don't think he got enough credit for what he's been doing, but Shai is a very, very great player and hopefully he continues for us and keeps getting better.

Ranchi, why did you change your nature this drastically? You've always been at least a little helpful but today you betrayed us, the bowlers screamed! Oh come on, if Roston Chase can, so can others. Stop bothering about me and see what best you can do, exclaimed the pitch. Seriously though, batting was easy once the dew set in. However, the bowlers still could have turned up better and asked more questions. It unfortunately turned out to be one of those modern days classics that is ruthless on the bowlers. Will we see an even contest between bat and ball in the next game? Oh ho! The next game is in Indore folks! The bowlers might well want to just put their feet up and ask them to use bowling machines. Because hey, those tiny boundaries and that placid pitch are no fun to bowl on! Will the curators have mercy on the bowlers and make batting challenging? Lots to look forward to on Sunday.
